questions.stem: Two standard dice are placed on a table, with one on top of the other, so that only nine of the faces of the dice may be seen. The touching faces have the same number on them. The sum of the numbers on the visible faces is 33. What is the number on the touching faces?

The length of a rectangular piece of paper is three times its width. The paper is folded so that one vertex lies on top of the opposite vertex, thus forming a pentagonal shape. What is the area of the pentagon as a fraction of the area of the original rectangle?

The number $M=124563987$ is the smallest number which uses all the non-zero digits once each and which has the property that none of the pairs of its consecutive digits makes a prime number. For example, the 5th and 6th digits of $M$ make the number 63 which is not prime. $N$ is the largest number which uses all the non-zero digits once each and which has the property that none of the pairs of its consecutive digits makes a prime number. What are the 5th and 6th digits of $N$?
Three semicircles, each of area 24, overlap as shown in the diagram. The centres of the arcs are $X$, $Y$ and $Z$ and $\angle ZXY=30^\circ$. What is the total area of the shaded regions?

figures.alt: Two semicircles stand on a common horizontal line: one centred at X, and one centred at Y where Y is the right-hand end of the first one's diameter (XY = r). A third semicircle, centred at Z, has its diameter on the line from X at 30° above the horizontal, starting at X; Z lies on the arc of the semicircle centred at X. Shaded: the three regions lying in exactly two of the semicircles.

questions.stem: The diagram shows two squares, $OPQR$ and $OSTU$. Point $S$ lies on $QV$. Triangle $UQV$ is isosceles with a right angle at $V$. Square $OPQR$ has area 25. What is the area of square $OSTU$?

figures.alt: Square OSTU on the left (U bottom-left, O bottom-right, S top-right, T top-left) and smaller square OPQR on the right sharing vertex O (O bottom-left, P bottom-right, Q top-right, R top-left), with U, O, P on one horizontal line and R on OS. V is above TS; triangle UQV has a right angle at V, and S lies on QV.

questions.stem: In the diagram, the outer hexagon is regular and has an area of 216. What is the shaded area?

figures.alt: A regular hexagon with its six short diagonals drawn, forming a six-pointed star; the small regular hexagon at the centre of the star is shaded.

questions.stem: As shown in the diagram, triangle $FGH$ is divided into four smaller triangles which have areas 4, 8, 12 and 8 respectively. What is the area of triangle $IKH$?

figures.alt: Triangle FGH: G far left, F at the top, H at the bottom-right. I lies on FH near H; J and K lie on FG (J nearer F). Segments IJ, IK and IG are drawn, making four triangles: FJI (area 4), JKI (8), KGI (12) and GHI (8). Triangle IKH is not drawn.

questions.stem: Alitta claims that if $p$ is an odd prime then $p^2-2$ is also an odd prime. Which of the following values of $p$ is a counterexample to this claim?
The diagram shows an equilateral triangle divided into nine smaller equilateral triangles, with two additional lines. What fraction of the large triangle is shaded?

figures.alt: Large equilateral triangle divided into 9 small equilateral triangles (3 rows: 1, 3, 5). Two extra straight lines cut across it; the shaded regions are two thin triangles, each spanning across small triangles, one in the upper-left and one along the bottom.

questions.stem: The plane can be tiled using the ‘hat tile’ shown here. This tile can be subdivided into eight congruent kites. The area of the hat tile is $8\sqrt3$. What is the perimeter of the hat tile?

figures.alt: The ‘hat’ aperiodic tile: an irregular 13-sided polygon made of eight congruent kites (thin internal lines show the kites).
